checks: The nonzero dot products give strict cap signs at the endpoint. A small neighborhood preserves every sign and isolates the integer base.
Unique exposure and compactness give a strict gap on the complement of the neighborhood. The positive-part hinge is globally finite and convex, and its positive set on C is inside that neighborhood.

With y interior, the gauge of the translated fiber is finite and continuous by its inball bound and subadditivity. The radial endpoint map is continuous. Radial projection on the boundary is Lipschitz because the radius is bounded below, so a positive spherical patch implies positive local boundary measure. In d=1 the exposed endpoint contributes one counted atom.
All integer-fiber boundary measures are finite. On the positive set the profile is exactly W(X), giving equality of the efficiency with W(X).

Strict convexity makes any supporting hyperplane at a fiber endpoint have a single contact. The two opposite endpoints have complementary strict signs, giving a profile value of at least one half at one endpoint.

overlap.comparison: That construction uses a selector of marked facet normals and exposure in one incident lifted simplex facet. Here there is one hinge on the unmarked entire boundary measure, with ambient exposure and arbitrary convex fibers, and a strict-convexity corollary. The marked selector theorem does not imply this claim.

readability: The two boundary-measure cases and the unmarked nature of the hinge are explicit.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: A unique exposed ambient maximizer localizes a single unmarked affine hinge on the strict profile of its boundary ray. The strict-convexity corollary follows by selecting the better opposite ray.
